C038.year_line: 2009 · Mint: Slovakia euro issue (Kremnica / national side)
C038.metal: copper-plated steel · 3.06 g · 18.75 mm · plain with groove · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip
C038.design: national Kriváň peak · double-cross arms + SLOVENSKO · date · 12 EU stars · common Europe map side (Luc Luycx) · Drahomír Zobek
C038.label: Slovakia · 2009 · 2 Euro Cent
C038.notes: SER EU-SK-001. Country #12. SLOVENSKO · Kriváň peak · double-cross arms · 2009 · 12 EU stars. First calendar year Slovakia used the euro (1 Jan 2009). Sole Slovakia · SER EU-SK-001. Slovakia flips now 1.
C038.story: A 2009 Slovak 2-euro-cent coin. Slovakia's side shows Kriváň, a famous peak in the Tatra mountains, with the Slovak double cross and the word SLOVENSKO, designed by Drahomír Zobek. The other side, shared by every euro country, was designed by Luc Luycx. Struck in copper-plated steel.

C285.label: Slovakia · 2009 · 5 Euro Cent
C285.notes: Phase 1 from the national side only; denomination from the measured size (1, 2 and 5 cent share the design). Confirm at Phase 2 from the value side.
C285.story: A 2009 five-cent euro coin from Slovakia, from the year Slovakia joined the euro. The national side shows the peak of Kriváň in the Tatra mountains with SLOVENSKO, the date and the Slovak coat of arms, inside the twelve stars of Europe.
